source: Approximate on-demand list prices for us-central1 (Tier 1) from cloud.google.com/sql/pricing (Enterprise edition), cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/pricing (M1 capacity band) and cloud.google.com/run/pricing (instance-based billing), cross-checked against published third-party price lists

items.label: Cloud Run worker pool vCPU (always on)
Cloud Run worker pool memory (per GiB, always on)

fixed.label: VPC, Private Service Access and Direct VPC egress

notes: Approximate on-demand list prices, 730 h/month, us-central1; before taxes, sustained/committed-use discounts and the Cloud Run free tier.
multiplier_variable/multipliers: the item total is multiplied by multipliers[value of that variable] (missing value = 1). REGIONAL (HA) Cloud SQL doubles instance and storage cost.

per_unit_variable: the item is multiplied by the numeric value of that variable divided by per_unit_divisor. per_unit_unit "GiB" means the value is a Kubernetes-style quantity to convert to GiB first: "512Mi" = 0.5, "2Gi" = 2, a bare number = GiB.

Cloud Run worker pools are priced with the instance-based (CPU always allocated) vCPU-second and GiB-second rates ($0.000018 and $0.000002); Google advertises worker pools as cheaper, so treat these lines as an upper bound.
Memorystore uses the M1 (1-4 GB) per-GB rate; larger capacities are billed at lower per-GB rates, so big instances are overestimated.
Shared-core Cloud SQL tiers (db-f1-micro, db-g1-small) are not covered by the Cloud SQL SLA. Custom tiers are priced at $0.0413 per vCPU-hour and $0.007 per GB-hour of memory.
Not included: backups and point-in-time-recovery logs, network egress, Cloud Logging above the free allotment, Artifact Registry storage.
